title: Help has to become available

character.name: Mira
character.goal: finish the story she is writing about a fox who steals the moon
character.anchor: the fox and the missing moon
character.opening:
Mira loves making up stories. Her newest one is about a fox who steals the moon. She knows exactly how it begins. The ending is still scattered across three notebooks.

One evening, her father sits beside her while she searches for the page she needs. ‘I know what happens next,’ she says. ‘I just keep losing where I am.’ He stays at the table. For once, finishing the assignment becomes less urgent than understanding what makes it difficult.

chapters.title: Help has to become available
chapters.narration: Mira and her father turn from naming the difficulty to finding someone they can speak with. A question written on paper does not put an appointment on a calendar. They make room for the practical questions: who can they reach, what support is available, and how can they begin a conversation? A second page takes shape beside the unfinished project. It holds the questions they want to bring to someone who can help them think through the next step.

chapters.title: Bring the question back to the day
chapters.narration: Mira brings the conversation about symptom severity back to the kitchen table. The discussion becomes more specific: which parts of an ordinary day feel difficult, and how do those difficulties interrupt something that matters? The wish to finish the story she is writing about a fox who steals the moon gives the question a concrete shape. This is where the route moves toward everyday functioning. The discussion moves beyond naming concerns to asking what they interrupt: participation, a task, an idea that the character wants to carry through.

chapters.title: An ending worth reaching
chapters.narration: The questions about functional impairment bring us back to the fox and the missing moon. Mira's goal has stayed with the story even as the conversation moved through several different concepts. The destination is a day with room for the things the character cares about. There is still a project on the table and a future to work out. The story arrives here because the goal was always larger than a label or an appointment: making room for an ordinary life that feels meaningful to the person living it.
